overview.title: Welcome to Agadir — Atlantic beach and a city rebuilt for the sun
overview.p1: Agadir sits on Morocco’s central Atlantic coast, about three hours southwest of Marrakech. After the 1960 earthquake the centre was rebuilt as a modern grid: wide avenues, a long public beach and a marina. What remains of the old kasbah crowns the hill with a wide view over the bay.
overview.p2: Beyond the shore: Souk El Had for everyday shopping, Taghazout for surf villages to the north, Paradise Valley in the Anti-Atlas foothills, Crocoparc and the Souss-Massa wetlands for nature. This is beach Morocco with easy logistics — not a medina maze.

places.title: Must-visit places in Agadir
places.subtitle: Beach, viewpoint, marina, souk and nearby coast.

beach.title: Agadir Beach
beach.desc: Long public Atlantic sand with a wide promenade — the city’s main outdoor space.

kasbah.title: Kasbah Agadir Oufella
kasbah.desc: Hilltop ruins and panorama over the bay — the classic Agadir photo stop.

marina.title: Agadir Marina
marina.desc: Yacht basin, cafés and evening stroll between the beach and the port.

souk.title: Souk El Had
souk.desc: One of Morocco’s largest weekly markets — produce, spices and everyday goods.

corniche.title: Corniche
corniche.desc: Seafront walk linking beach hotels, cafés and the marina strip.

taghazout.title: Taghazout
taghazout.desc: Surf village north of Agadir — relaxed beach days and Atlantic waves.

paradise.title: Paradise Valley
paradise.desc: Palm gorges and natural pools in the Anti-Atlas foothills inland from Agadir.

crocoparc.title: Crocoparc
crocoparc.desc: Crocodile park and gardens south of the city — popular half-day outing.

birds.title: Souss-Massa Birds
birds.desc: Wetlands and bird reserve along the Souss estuary and national park coast.

directory.title: Find your ideal stay in Agadir
directory.subtitle: Beach hotels, marina apartments and stays near Taghazout.

eat.title: Where to eat in Agadir
eat.subtitle: Seafood on the marina, beach cafés and simple grills near the souk.

nomad.title: Marina tables
nomad.desc: Fish and seafood with harbour views.

jardin.title: Beach cafés
jardin.desc: Casual drinks and snacks along the promenade.

moha.title: Simple grills
moha.desc: Everyday Moroccan plates near Souk El Had.

fassia.title: Hotel restaurants
fassia.desc: Reliable options on the seafront strip.

elfenn.title: City centre
elfenn.desc: Cafés and tagines away from the beach crowds.

bacha.title: Port catch
bacha.desc: Fresh fish when the boats are in.

transport.title: Getting around
transport.desc: Petit taxis cover the city and beach strip. Buses and shared taxis link Taghazout; agree prices for Paradise Valley day trips.

bargain.title: Sun & wind
bargain.desc: Agadir is one of Morocco’s sunniest cities — high SPF on the beach. Wind is milder than Essaouira but evenings can cool.

water.title: Cash & cards
water.desc: Cards work in hotels and larger restaurants. Carry dirhams for taxis, souk stalls and small cafés.

daytrips.title: Best day trips from Agadir
daytrips.subtitle: Surf coast, palm valleys and nature parks within easy reach.

taghazout.title: Taghazout & surf beaches
taghazout.desc: About 20–30 minutes north along the coast.

paradise.title: Paradise Valley
paradise.desc: Palm gorge and pools about 1–1.5 hours inland.

crocoparc.title: Crocoparc
crocoparc.desc: Crocodile park south of the city — half-day outing.

mass.title: Souss-Massa coast
mass.desc: Wetlands and quieter beaches toward the national park.

q1.question: How many days in Agadir?
q1.answer: Two full days cover the beach, kasbah, marina and souk. Three to four days allow Taghazout, Paradise Valley or Crocoparc.

q2.question: Is Agadir only a beach resort?
q2.answer: The beach is central, but the kasbah viewpoint, Souk El Had, marina and nearby nature trips add variety beyond the sand.

q3.question: How do I get to Agadir?
q3.answer: Agadir Al Massira Airport (AGA) has domestic and international flights. Buses and private transfers link Marrakech (≈3 hours) and Casablanca.

q4.question: Best time to visit Agadir?
q4.answer: Spring and autumn for warm beach days without peak summer heat. Winter is mild; summer is hot and busy.

q5.question: Is Taghazout far from Agadir?
q5.answer: About 20–30 minutes by road north of the city — easy as a day trip or a surf-base stay.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-day itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: Beach, viewpoint and one day trip.

day1.title: Day 1 — Beach & Kasbah
day1.desc: Morning on Agadir Beach and the corniche. Afternoon up to Kasbah Agadir Oufella for the bay view. Evening at the Marina.

day2.title: Day 2 — Souk & Marina
day2.desc: Souk El Had in the morning. Afternoon free for the beach or marina cafés. Optional sunset from the kasbah hill.

day3.title: Day 3 — Coast or valley
day3.desc: Choose Taghazout for surf beaches, Paradise Valley for palm gorges, or Crocoparc for a family half-day.

d1.m: Beach walk and coffee on the corniche.
d1.a: Taxi or walk up to the Kasbah viewpoint.

d2.m: Souk El Had — spices, produce and crafts.

d3.m: Depart for Taghazout, Paradise Valley or Crocoparc.
d3.e: Last evening on the beach strip.
